This chapter serves as a space for professional and creative development and focuses on cultivating community for any student interested in/aspiring to be in the media industry.

name: Rutgers Newark Chess Club
description: Welcome to the first Official Chess Organization at The University of Rutgers-Newark! We are the Raider Rooks, and our mission here is to provide students with a comfortable but competitive environment through the widely-known sport of chess. We plan to allow students the opportunity to challenge themselves through this complex yet intriguing game while simultaneously building a collective and easy-going community that respects all individuals, their beliefs, and ways of life. So come join and help us promote the game of chess!

name: Rutgers Newark Student Governing Association 201
description: The RUN-SGA is a group of dedicated student leaders who serve the interests of all undergraduates, part-time and full-time on the Newark Campus. The RUNSGA represents the Newark College of Arts and Sciences, Rutgers Business School, School or Public Affairs and Administration, and School of Criminal Justice. What does the RUN-SGA actually do? The mission of the RUN-SGA is to serve and protect the interests of its student population on the Newark Campus. We face a plethora of issues each semester and help address them by meeting with campus administrators, faculty, and staff.

name: Rutgers Newark Swim Club
description: The Rutgers–Newark Swim Club is dedicated to promoting water safety, confidence, and lifelong swimming skills by providing inclusive, supportive, and accessible swim instruction for students and community members of all backgrounds and abilities.

name: Rutgers Newark Young Democratic Socialists of America
description: Our mission is to educate and organize students and young people and to play a helpful and principled role in the movement for social justice. Within and throughout this struggle, we will articulate and defend the idea that true human liberation is impossible under capitalism. We seek social change which extends democracy into all aspects of life -- social, political and economic. This is the struggle for democratic socialism. Our vision of socialism is profoundly democratic, feminist, and anti-racist.

name: Rutgers Quantitative Finance Club
description: The Quantitative Finance Club at Rutgers University–Newark builds a strong, inquisitive, and motivated community of scholars interested in mathematics, finance, and data-driven problem-solving. Our mission is to create a place where ambitious students can explore the analytical underpinning of modern markets, develop technical skill, and gain the confidence they need to succeed in the competitive financial world. name: Rutgers Real Estate Society
description: The purpose of the real estate society shall be to educate the student body on the Real Estate industry. The Rutgers Real Estate Club is a place for people interested in Real Estate, Internships, and Everything Business to come together and learn from experienced speakers in the industry and from each other. The society also provides networking and internship opportunities. WE ACCEPT ALL STUDENTS, BUSINESS OR NOT!

name: Rutgers Student Veteran Organization
description: The Rutgers Student Veteran Organization empowers student veterans to achieve academic excellence, secure elite professional outcomes, and become influential campus and community leaders. We accomplish this by providing structured peer mentorship, career development pathways, unwavering advocacy for veteran-specific needs, and a powerful sense of camaraderie rooted in shared service.

name: Rutgers Students for Justice in Palestine
description: As a solidarity group, Rutgers Students for Justice in Palestine believes in the power of activism to educate Rutgers University-Newark about the ongoing plight of the Palestinian people as well as their history and cultural heritage. Furthermore, RSJP seeks to promote the Palestinian right to education and to foster communication with Palestinian schools and scholars. In the spirit of free expression, RSJP seeks to provide an alternative perspective to existing narratives as well as to engage in constructive dialogue, discussion and coalition building with other Rutgers student organizations.

name: Rutgers Undergraduate Women in Business
description: Rutgers Undergraduate Women in Business or "RUWIB" is a club that supports and encourages professional women in the business community. RU WIB is committed to encouraging personal growth for the student body through social events and opportunities where they will be able to network with fellow Rutgers students, alumni, faculty, administrators, and leaders in the outside business community. name: Rutgers University-Newark Hallyu Club
description: RU-N Hallyu Club is a student organization that focuses on global rise of Korean culture including K-Pop, K-Dramas, Korean fashion, Korean food, Korean entertainment and more! RU-N Hallyu Club also has a K-pop dance team, Haneul Dance Team, that's always open for new members of all skill levels! The club aims to create a diverse community of members who share an appreciation for the Korean Wave and to continually expand its network of members. discord: https://discord.gg/Md9PcMC6

name: Rutgers-Newark Student Chapter of the Society of Exploration Geophysicists
description: The mission of the Rutgers Newark Geophysical Society of Exploration Geophysicists student chapter is to promote interest in geophysics and to enhance collaboration and knowledge amongst those interested in the geophysical sciences. We accomplish these goals by holding regular meetings, organizing invited speakers, subsidizing members travel to meetings, and conducting field research with an emphasis on community outreach.

description: Sigma Beta Rho is a national multicultural Fraternity based upon the principles of Society, Brotherhood, and Remembrance. These pillars were established upon the formation of the Beta Chapter at the State University of New York, Binghamton, on August 16, 1996 and continue to guide our brotherhood to this day. description: Sigma Lambda Beta (ΣΛΒ) is a social fraternity established on cultural understanding and wisdom. Founded on April 4, 1986 at the University of Iowa, Iowa City, Iowa, the organization is committed to create and expand multicultural leadership, promote academic excellence, advance cultural awareness and service while influencing its mission amongst all dedicated collegiate men worldwide. description: Sigma Lambda Upsilon/Señoritas Latinas Unidas Sorority, Inc. highly prides itself as an organization of diverse collegiate and professional women dedicated to uplifting traditionally marginalized groups, specifically Latinos and women, by serving as a voice and means for empowerment. Since 1987, the Hermandad has been an outlet for professional development and personal growth to its members and serving constituents. name: Sikh Student Association
description: The Sikh Student Association is an organization dedicated to spreading knowledge about the Sikh religion and Punjabi culture through exciting awareness and Bhangra dance events. Our organization promotes diversity and unity within the community and hosts events that would work towards achieving that.

This is not limited to just East Asia, but also Southeast Asian countries that may fit this criteria. The SUSA shall exist for the following purposes: 1. name: SO-RAH
description: SO-RAH is dedicated to combating hunger, reducing food waste, advocating for the homeless by organizing events such as sandwich drives, food recoveries, food drives, clothing drives, educational events, and other activities to help out our local and school communities. Many people throughout the United States experience some type of food insecurity. name: Social Work Student Organization
description: The Social Work Student Organization (SWSO) is a student organization created for and by the social work students of Rutgers University. SWSO is committed to raising awareness and promoting activities that enhance the lives of others within our campus and communities, always reflecting the core values of the social work profession as designated by the National Association of Social Workers (NASW). Additionally, our goal is provide support and access to information and resources for all students pursuing a career in social work. We welcome all students from all majors!

name: Society for Corporate Law & Governance
description: The Society of Corporate Law and Governance builds a powerful campus network, connecting members with leading firms, distinguished professors, and influential alumni to unlock high-impact career opportunities. We equip our members with the precise skills, executive presence, and refined credentials needed to excel in competitive interviews and stand out to top recruiters. Through targeted professional development, peer mentorship, and exclusive networking events, we ensure our membership achieves maximum polish and readiness for the corporate legal world.

name: Society for Education Advocacy and Law (SEAL)
description: The purpose of SEAL is to provide a forum for students passionate about education law and policy to engage with critical issues affecting public education. SEAL envisions a future where quality public education is a right accessible to all individuals, fostering equity, growth, and opportunity within every community. We define quality education through our Core Four Pillars: 1. name: Society for Real Estate Law
description: SOREL's mission is to foster a deeper understanding of real estate law by exploring its complexities and evolving landscape through insightful discussions of legal concepts and current developments in the field.

name: South Asian Law Students Association
description: SALSA aims to provide an organizational framework to address issues of concern to the South Asian community, to ensure a support system for the South Asian law student community at Rutgers Law, and to build awareness of the South Asian experience within the law school community through its board, members, programs, resources, and functions.

name: STEM Club
description: The National Science Foundation developed the LSAMP (Louis Stokes Alliance for Minority Participation) to increase the number of professionals from minority groups who are traditionally underrepresented in the STEM fields. The Garden State LSAMP (GS-LSAMP) program provides New Jersey students interested in non-medical STEM fields with a supportive learning community and access to extensive resources to facilitate academic and career success. name: Street Law
description: Street Law’s programs and materials aim to help advance justice by empowering people with legal and civic knowledge, skills, and confidence to bring about positive change for themselves and others.

name: Student Association of Global Affairs 544
description: The purpose of the Student Association of Global Affairs (SAGA) is to enhance the learning environment for graduate students by facilitating and promoting communication and cooperation among and between Global Affairs graduate students, the Division of Global Affairs (DGA), faculty and staff affiliated with DGA, the greater Rutgers University academic community, and practitioners in the field.

name: Student Bar Association
description: The Student Bar Association is the umbrella organization for all other organizations in the law school. Extracurricular affairs of the school are governed by the SBA, which consists of elected representatives from each class, chosen on a proportional basis; these representatives elect officers to govern the association.

name: Student Health Services
description: The skilled doctors and nurses of Student Health Services are here to help you stay healthy. All students can meet with a medical professional to discuss preventative care and treatment options for illness. We also have a pharmacy for you to easily fill your prescriptions or grab over-the-counter items you may need in a pinch! Whether you need a well visit, a sick visit, or have questions about your health, you have a caring team of professionals ready to serve you!

name: Student Senate
description: Rutgers University School of Nursing Student Senate is the official student governance of RUSON. Our organization encourages active participation of nursing students professionally, academically and socially through career events, internal class activities and community volunteering opportunities.

name: Tax Law Sciety
description: Our mission is to serve as a resource for students interested in learning more about professional opportunities surrounding a career in taxation, and the various career paths available to a tax attorney.

name: The Honors College Student Council
description: The Honors College Student Council is a student run organization that collaborates with the Honors College and the Office of Student Life and Leadership to offer opportunities that help ALL Rutgers Newark students by providing opportunities for leadership and service. We organize numerous events each semester to help students fulfill their Honors College events and volunteering requirements. We also aspire to foster a sense of camaraderie both among members of the Honors College and the greater Rutgers Newark community.

name: The Observer
description: We are the independent student newspaper of Rutgers-Newark. We bring you the news on all things Rutgers and with your voice and ours, we make a difference.

name: The Rutgers Black Professionals Network
description: The Rutgers Black Professionals Network was created to help students achieve pre-professional opportunities and build an interdisciplinary community. We will advocate for professionalism, enable networking opportunities, and assist students in reaching their academic and personal goals. Through professional and leadership development workshops, student-professional mentorship, mixers, and engagement with alums, mentors, professors, and working professionals, we guide students on their distinct career paths. name: Tort Law
description: To educate, inform and connect Rutgers Law - Newark students with the Personal Injury, Medical Malpractice industry, and all other areas of Tort Law by increasing networking opportunities, hosting seminars and workshops and building relationships with affiliated organizations.

name: Transfer Student Organization
description: The Transfer Student Organization (TSO) is an organization founded by transfer students for transfer students, with the aim of providing a tailored college experience. We host a range of professional development events, info sessions, and social activities designed specifically for transfer students. Our goal is to create an incredible community for transfer students at RUN!

name: Turkish Student Association
description: The RU-TSA proposes the following to be its objectives: To promote the exchange of ideas for a better understanding of Turkish people, their culture and history, to present the interests of its members in dealing with the Rutgers University Administration and the various student organizations, and to provide an environment for interaction among its members and their families, international communities, Rutgers University students and staff and similar college associations.

name: Turning Point USA
description: Our Turning Point USA chapter's mission is to identify, educate, train, and organize students to promote the principles of fiscal responsibility, free markets, and limited government. We aim to guide citizens through the development of knowledge, skills, values, and motivation, so they can meaningfully engage in their communities to restore traditional American values like patriotism, respect for life, liberty, family, and fiscal responsibility. name: Undergraduate Student Organization Treasurers
description: A group for current student organization treasurers to share ideas, discuss policies, and connect for overall best practices for registered student organizations.

name: Undergraduate Student Organizations Presidents Group
description: A group for the Presidents of all undergraduate student organizations

name: Unicef
description: The mission of the UNICEF Club at Rutgers–Newark is to mobilize students to advocate for, support, and improve the lives of children, both globally and within the Newark community, by advancing UNICEF’s mission through education, service, fundraising, and local partnerships. The club seeks to raise awareness of issues affecting children while translating global UNICEF initiatives into meaningful, community-based action at the local level.

name: Violence Prevention & Victim Assistance
description: The Office for Violence Prevention and Victim Assistance (VPVA) focuses on educating our campus community about interpersonal violence (sexual violence, partner violence, stalking, and harassment), so that we can effectively prevent violence in all its forms. We also serve to support and empower those on our campus who have been affected by interpersonal violence, connect them with resources, and provide trauma-informed advocacy and services. Our goal is to have each member of our campus community feel safe, connected and have the tools to grow and heal. VPVA serves as a confidential resource

name: Women's Law Forum
description: The Women's Law Forum (WLF) is a collective committed to discussing, promoting, and advocating for women's issues. WLF provides a forum to explore the diversity of women's experiences, including differences of race, class, national origin, and sexuality. WLF challenges and works to eliminate the inherent gender bias of the legal system. WLF actively works toward building coalitions with other organizations to advance common goals and encourages the involvement of all women in the law school community. WLF seeks to educate the law school community on legal issues facing women throughout society

name: WRNU
description: WRNU is Rutgers Newark's on-campus radio station! Listen to us LIVE 24/7 on our website (www.wrnu.rutgers.edu) for the latest on social issues, news, music, politics, culture, love, and much more from students' voices. We play your favorite music from Hip-Hop, R&B, Afrobeat, Pop, Dance, Latin & More! WRNU also highlights the best of Rutgers Newark's very own, supporting aspiring artists, performers and creatives on our various platforms.
